- When sentiment is negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0), model often overshoots upward — cap forecast peaks early, especially if sentiment is strong but short-lived.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon — increase forecast by 1–2% for spikes > 5% from recent mean.  
- Model shows strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect momentum.  
- Mean reversion is overestimated — if price is above 3σ from 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion.  
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., >0.3 avg), model often fails to capture volatility — add 0.5–1.0% volatility buffer to forecast range.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to forecast flat — introduce 0.5–1.0% upward bias to account for hidden market momentum.
